public_body: Fall River City Council Committee On Finance
overall: The AG found one violation: the July 28 executive session topic on the notice lacked enough detail for the public to understand the discussion. The other four allegations (access, invited attendees, executive session purpose, recording announcement) were not violations.

allegations.summary: Committee met in person on July 28 without allowing members of the public to physically attend; public could only watch remotely.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee provided adequate, alternative access to the July 28 meeting, and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee let the Mayor, Police Chief and Director of Financial Services attend in person while other members of the public had to watch remotely.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by allowing three Fall River city officials to attend the July 28 meeting in person, while requiring other members of the public to view the meeting remotely.

allegations.summary: Executive session topic was improperly added or amended within 48 hours of the July 28 meeting, and the original topic lacked sufficient detail.
Committee convened in executive session on July 28 for an improper purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We find that, overall, the discussions in executive session were appropriate under Purpose 4 as they related to public safety and the deployment of security personnel or devices.

allegations.summary: Chair did not adequately announce that the July 28 meeting was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reasons expressed in those determinations, we also find no violation here as the chair’s statement satisfied the requirement that he inform attendees of any recording.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
